lines.d1: Asking a disk-based database for the same data again and again is slow.
lines.d2: Redis keeps data in memory, so reads and writes are extremely fast.
lines.d3: As a cache: check Redis first. On a miss, load from the database and store the result.
lines.d4: A time to live expires old entries, so the cache does not serve stale data forever.
lines.d5: It is more than key and value: strings, lists, sets, sorted sets, and hashes.
lines.d6: That powers sessions, rate limits, queues, and leaderboards.
